commons.credit: C. Hart Merriam Collection of Native American Photographs, X. SHOSHONE STOCK Monache Piute Western Monache 23d. Nim or Monache Nim at North Fork; 1902.
commons.description: The Western Mono (or Nim) lived in the southern Sierra Nevada's western foothills, covering Madera, Fresno, and Tulare counties in the San Joaquin Valley, near rivers like the San Joaquin, Kings, and Kaweah. They led a semi-nomadic life, mainly focusing on fishing, hunting, gathering and limited agriculture.
commons.editorial_reason: Caption/source identify the people as Western Mono, and the image shows a Mono group with woven baskets and traditional material culture.
